papers_read.title_as_printed: Psychosocial profiles within community-dwelling older adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment: A prevalence and latent profile analysis study (Siew et al., Asian J Psychiatry 2023)
Association of Qi-stagnation constitution and subjective sleep characteristics with mild cognitive impairment among elderly in community: A cross-sectional study (Liu et al., Eur J Integr Med 2023)

what_each_reports.P-259: Singapore CHI study, 902 community-dwelling adults aged 60-99; Petersen-criteria MCI by consensus panel after a nine-subdomain battery; MCI prevalence 21.5% (194 MCI, 696 normal, 12 dementia). MCI group had fewer years of education, lower perceived social support and higher GDS scores (small effects). Latent profile analysis on 166 MCI: positive 45.2%, neutral 38.5%, negative 16.3%.
what_each_reports.P-261: Fuzhou, 1,071 non-depressed adults aged 55-75 (GDS-15 > 8 excluded); MoCA-based MCI prevalence 29.3%. Adjusted OR 2.581 (1.706-3.907) for MCI with joint sleep disturbance and Qi-stagnation vs neither.

quantity_a: Point prevalence of Petersen/DSM-5 mild NCD in Singapore community adults 60-99 (and group differences in psychosocial scores).
quantity_b: Adjusted odds ratio of MoCA-defined MCI for joint sleep disturbance and Qi-stagnation vs neither, in non-depressed Fuzhou adults 55-75.
incompatible_if_same: Not applicable: a prevalence and an odds ratio are different quantities. On the constructs both touch, they agree: both find lower education in MCI (P-259 t = 2.04, p = .038; P-261 education median 9 vs 11 years, p < 0.001). The prevalence figures (21.5% vs 29.3%) are from different age bands, countries and diagnostic procedures, and neither paper claims the other's population rate.

gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Singapore CHI vs Fuzhou community day-care centres; the record itself sets dataset_equal = No

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: prevalence proportion vs odds ratio for an exposure; MCI defined by Petersen criteria and consensus (P-259) vs MoCA cut-offs plus clinical criteria (P-261)
independence: Distinct studies, different countries and authors.
grounds: P-259's figure is a prevalence (21.5%) of consensus-diagnosed MCI in Singaporeans aged 60-99.
P-261's figure is an adjusted odds ratio (2.581) for a joint sleep and TCM-constitution exposure in Fuzhou adults aged 55-75.
A prevalence and an odds ratio are different metric types; population, diagnostic procedure and exposure also differ, and the record already fails its own dataset gate.
Where the two papers address the same construct (education), their results point the same way.

evidence_quotes.quote: The prevalence of MCI in our sample was 21.5%. They had significantly lower years of education and perceived social support and higher depressive symptoms than the normal ageing group.
Objective cognitive impairment criterion was operationalized as scoring 1.5 standard deviations below the age and education appropriate norms in any of the tests in the neurocognitive battery
the risk of suffering from MCI for older adults with sleep disturbance and Qi-stagnation was 2.581 times higher than that for those without sleep disturbance or Qi-stagnation
Among the 1071 study subjects, 314 suffered from MCI, with a prevalence rate of 29.3%.

record_defects: gap_magnitude 0.189 is computed between a percentage (21.5%) and an odds ratio (2.581), which is meaningless.
The PDF map titles P-261 as a speech-analysis paper; the PDF text is the Liu et al. Qi-stagnation/sleep study the record means.
resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' implies a disagreement bridged by third studies; there is no disagreement, and the 'bridging' papers (P-262 HR 8.52) explain nothing.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these two papers; a comparison would need the same metric (e.g. two prevalences under the same MCI criteria and age band with non-overlapping CIs).
